teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner expresses frustration over English irregular spellings.
💡 Solution: Provide historical explanation: Spelling is 15th-century historical heritage, not random error.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Historical Phonology, Vowel Shifts & Archaic Spellings
1. Definition: Modern English spelling reflects 15th-century Middle English pronunciation prior to major historical sound shifts.

2. Rule: The Great Vowel Shift raised all long vowels (e.g. /iː/ -> /aɪ/ in bite; /uː/ -> /aʊ/ in house) while printing standardized pre-shift spelling. Silent letters (doubt, sign, walk, hour) represent historic consonants or Renaissance etymological restorations.
3. Why? Caxton's printing press in 1476 frozen English spelling right before the sound system underwent massive transformation.
4. How to recognize? Irregular long vowel spellings and etymological silent letters.
5. Common examples: bite (historically /biːtə/ -> now /baɪt/), house (historically /huːs/ -> now /haʊs/), doubt /daʊt/ (b inserted from Latin dubitandum), sign /saɪn/ (g silent before n)
6. Counter-examples: Modern phonetic coinages and acronyms.
7. Exceptions: Dialectal survivals in regional English.
8. Common mistakes: Viewing English spelling as random rather than historical.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: English spelling is a 500-year-old photograph of spoken English!
10. Key vocabulary: Great Vowel Shift, historical orthography, Caxton printing, etymological silent letter, diachronic linguistics
11. Frequency: ★★★☆☆ (Specialist)
12. CEFR Level: ⚫ C2
13. Associated Visual: 📜 Historical timeline showing 1400 spelling frozen while 1600 speech shifted.
14. Key Takeaway: English spelling is a historical photograph of 15th-century speech!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Why does English spelling look different from its modern pronunciation? (Because spelling was frozen in the 15th century before the Great Vowel Shift)
CCQ 2: Why was the letter 'b' added to 'doubt'? (As a Renaissance etymological restoration from Latin dubitandum)
CCQ 3: What was the Great Vowel Shift? (A major historical change between 1400–1700 where long vowels shifted position)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Explain the historical origin of these irregular spellings:
🎯 Item: doubt (silent b) ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Latin etymological insertion (dubitandum)
🎯 Item: sign (silent g) ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: French/Latin root where g was silent before n
🎯 Item: bite (long vowel) ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Great Vowel Shift raised Middle English /iː/ to /aɪ/
